quote: Mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalomyopathy (MNGIE) is a progressive metabolic disorder caused by thymidine phosphorylase (TP) enzyme deficiency.
summary: Review of MNGIE caused by thymidine phosphorylase deficiency, with treatment options and gene therapy in mice; nothing on UC.

quote: Mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalomyopathy (MNGIE-MTDPS1) is a devastating autosomal recessive disorder due to mutations in TYMP, which cause a loss of function of thymidine phosphorylase (TP), nucleoside accumulation in plasma and tissues, and mitochondrial dysfunction.
summary: Review of MNGIE-MTDPS1, caused by loss-of-function TYMP mutations, covering clinical features, diagnosis and therapies; no UC content.
Review of neurological manifestations of gastrointestinal disorders that mentions MNGIE as a disease only; the TYMP gene is not discussed.

quote: Mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalomyopathy (MNGIE) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the gene encoding thymidine phosphorylase and is characterized by external ophthalmoparesis, gastrointestinal dysmotility, leukoencephalopathy, and neuropathy.
summary: Three atypical MNGIE patients with TYMP-related disease, one mimicking inflammatory intestinal disease; no UC association is reported.

quote: MNGIE is a rare and fatal disease in which absence of the enzyme thymidine phosphorylase induces systemic accumulation of thymidine and deoxyuridine and secondary mitochondrial DNA alterations.
summary: Review of gastrointestinal dysmotility and loss of interstitial cells of Cajal in MNGIE, which is caused by absent thymidine phosphorylase; no UC content.

quote: Mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalomyopathy (MNGIE) is an ultra-rare disease caused by mutations in TYMP, the gene encoding for the enzyme thymidine phosphorylase.
summary: Review of diagnosis and treatment of MNGIE caused by TYMP mutations; nothing on UC.

quote: The extension and distribution of leukoencephalopathy were not clearly linked with age, phenotype or disease severity, and did not seem to be related to TYMP mutations, enzyme activity or pyrimidine levels.
summary: In four MNGIE patients, brain MRI leukoencephalopathy was not clearly related to TYMP mutations or enzyme activity; not a UC study.

quote: MNGIE: Mitochondrial neuro-gastro-intestinal encephalopathy (MNGIE) is a rare (∼100 cases worldwide) AR, multisystem MID due to mutations in TYMP1 [ 95 ].
summary: Review of orphan neuropathies that briefly notes MNGIE is due to TYMP mutations; no UC content.

quote: Thirteen DEPs that were relatively highly expressed in the drug metabolism pathway were validated with parallel reaction monitoring (PRM), of which MPO, TYMP, IMPDH2, GSTM4, and ALDH3A1 were highly expressed in PV, whereas CES1, MAOB, MGST1, and GSTT1 were less expressed in PV.
summary: TYMP protein was higher in psoriasis vulgaris lesional skin than in healthy skin by proteomics and PRM; this is not a UC study.
Histology of the interstitial cell of Cajal network in an MNGIE patient; MNGIE is named as a disease and nothing is reported about the TYMP gene.

quote: The results of parallel reaction monitoring (PRM) analysis suggested that S100s, STAT1, KRT2, TYMP, SOD2, HSP90AB1, TFRC, and COL5A1 were the most significantly changed proteins in both groups.
summary: TYMP is one of several proteins that changed in psoriatic lesions on adalimumab or secukinumab; no specific result about it and not a UC study.

quote: A set of genes with "angiogenesis" GO term identified in a previous expression microarray experiment (SCG2, STAB1, TGFA, ANG, ERBB2, GNA13, PML, CASP8, ECGF1, JAG1, HIF1A, TNFSF13 and TGM2) was selected for genetic and functional studies.
summary: ECGF1 (TYMP) is one of thirteen angiogenesis genes studied in celiac disease; the reported findings concern other genes.

quote: Elevated plasma and urine thymidine and deoxyuridine, and genetic testing for TYMP variants, confirmed MNGIE.
summary: Two sisters diagnosed with Crohn's disease were found to have MNGIE with identical TYMP variants; a case report of a mimic, not an IBD association.

quote: Subsequent molecular genetic testing demonstrated a homozygous TYMP gene mutation.
summary: Case of MNGIE with a homozygous TYMP mutation that was first misdiagnosed as anorexia nervosa and Crohn's disease; not an IBD association.

quote: Markedly diminished thymidine phosphorylase activity and increased thymidine plasma levels confirmed the diagnosis of MNGIE.
summary: In a boy first suspected of Crohn disease, markedly low thymidine phosphorylase activity confirmed MNGIE; biopsies showed megamitochondria.

quote: An AAV8 vector carrying the human TYMP gene was administered in the left lobe with the right serving as a control.
summary: TYMP gene delivery cleared accumulated nucleosides in an explanted MNGIE patient liver; no inflammation or colitis outcome was measured.
Descriptive review of peripheral neuropathy in gastrointestinal disorders that mentions MNGIE only as a disease; the TYMP gene is not discussed.

quote: TYMP up-regulated IL-6, which activated tissue factor (TF), a primary trigger of the extrinsic coagulation cascade.
summary: In calciphylaxis, serum up-regulated TYMP in endothelial cells, which drove IL-6 and tissue factor signalling; not a UC study.
